# The Rock Fan Club — fan reference on Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson (2026)

This is an UNOFFICIAL fan site. It is not run by, affiliated with or endorsed by Dwayne Johnson, Seven Bucks or WME, and it does not speak for him. Facts below are compiled by fans from public sources.

Site: __SITE_URL__/
Fan club (unofficial): __SITE_URL__/fanclub.html
Write to the fan club: __SITE_URL__/contact.html (letters stay with the fan club; they are not forwarded to Dwayne Johnson or his team)

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Identity
- **Full Legal Name:** Dwayne Douglas Johnson
- **Ring & Stage Moniker:** The Rock / The People's Champion / The Final Boss
- **Born:** May 2, 1972 · Hayward, California, USA
- **Heritage:** Samoan and Black Canadian wrestling royalty — son of WWE Hall of Famer "Soul Man" Rocky Johnson (first Black WWF Tag Team Champion, 1983) and Ata Johnson; grandson of Samoan wrestling legend High Chief Peter Maivia and promoter Lia Maivia.
- **Education:** University of Miami (Bachelor of General Studies, Criminology & Physiology, 1995); Defensive Tackle (#94) on the 1991 NCAA National Championship Miami Hurricanes football team.
- **Global Box Office:** Over $14 billion worldwide across theatrical releases (2001–2026).
- **Dramatic Accolades:** Golden Globe Nominee (Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama) for portraying UFC pioneer Mark Kerr in Benny Safdie's A24 biographical drama *The Smashing Machine* (2025), which received a 15-minute standing ovation at the Venice Film Festival.
- **Corporate Governance:** Appointed to the Board of Directors of TKO Group Holdings (parent company of UFC and WWE) in January 2024, securing full ownership of "The Rock" trademark and intellectual property.

---

## 2. Career Chronology & Defining Reinventions
1. **Roots & Early Life (1972–1990):** Raised across Auckland (New Zealand), Hamden (Connecticut), Honolulu (Hawaii), Nashville, and Bethlehem (Pennsylvania). Evicted from a Honolulu efficiency apartment at age 14—a formative turning point that drove him to weight training and athletics under Coach Jody Cwik at Freedom High School.
2. **University of Miami & The "$7 Bucks" Crossroads (1990–1995):** Played 39 games (77 tackles, 4.5 sacks) at Miami and won the 1991 National Championship alongside future Hall of Famers such as Warren Sapp. After going undrafted in the 1995 NFL Draft and being cut from the CFL's Calgary Stampeders practice squad two months into the season, he returned home to Tampa with $7 in his pocket—later inspiring the name **Seven Bucks Productions**.
3. **WWE Attitude Era & Championship Legacy (1996–2004, 2011–2013, 2024–present):**
   - Debuted at WWF Survivor Series (November 1996) as Rocky Maivia.
   - Reinvented himself in 1997 as **The Rock**, becoming the youngest WWF Champion at the time (Survivor Series 1998) and headlining iconic WrestleMania main events against Stone Cold Steve Austin (XV, X-Seven, XIX), Hulk Hogan (X8), John Cena (XXVIII, 29), and teaming with Roman Reigns as "The Final Boss" at WrestleMania XL (2024).
   - **Championship Record:** 10× World Champion (8× WWF/WWE Champion, 2× WCW Champion), 2× Intercontinental Champion, 5× Tag Team Champion, 2000 Royal Rumble Winner, 6th WWE Triple Crown Champion.
4. **Hollywood Box Office Titan & Studio Builder (2001–2026):**
   - Broke out in *The Mummy Returns* (2001) and *The Scorpion King* (2002, Guinness World Record $5.5M debut lead salary), followed by *The Rundown* (2003), *Walking Tall* (2004), and *Gridiron Gang* (2006).
   - Co-founded **Seven Bucks Productions** with Dany Garcia in 2012, revitalizing *Fast & Furious* starting with *Fast Five* (2011) through *Furious 7* ($1.515B) and *Hobbs & Shaw* ($760M), anchoring *San Andreas* ($474M), Sony's *Jumanji: Welcome to the Jungle* ($962M) and *Jumanji: The Next Level* ($801M), Disney's *Moana* ($687M) and *Moana 2* ($1.06B+), *Jungle Cruise*, Netflix's *Red Notice*, *Black Adam*, A24's *The Smashing Machine* (2025), and Disney's live-action *Moana* (2026).

---

## 3. Founded Ventures & Ownership Portfolio
- **Seven Bucks Productions** — Co-Founder (with Dany Garcia). Global film, television, digital, and cultural studio. Official site: https://sevenbucks.com
- **Teremana Small Batch Tequila** — Founder & Chairman. Craft Highland agave tequila distilled in Jalisco, Mexico (NOM 1613), fastest-growing spirits launch in history (1M+ annual 9L cases). Official site: https://teremana.com
- **PAPATUI** — Founder. Formulated men's skin, body, hair, and tattoo care brand. Official site: https://papatui.com
- **ZOA Energy** — Co-Founder. Clean performance and zero-sugar energy beverages. Official site: https://zoaenergy.com
- **Project Rock** — Founder (in partnership with Under Armour). Performance footwear, apparel, and Iron Paradise training gear. Official site: https://www.underarmour.com/en-us/c/project-rock/
- **United Football League (UFL)** — Co-Owner. Professional spring American football league formed from the XFL–USFL merger. Official site: https://www.theufl.com
- **TKO Group Holdings** — Member of the Board of Directors (UFC & WWE parent company). Official site: https://tkogrp.com

## 4. Complete Motion Picture Filmography (2001–2026)
- **Longshot** (2001) — Role: *Mugger* · Directed by Lionel C. Martin · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/longshot
  A low-budget comedy produced by Lou Pearlman and packed with cameos from late-’90s pop acts. Johnson turns up briefly as a mugger.
- **The Mummy Returns** (2001) — Role: *Mathayus / The Scorpion King* · Directed by Stephen Sommers · Worldwide Box Office: $433M · Critics Score: 46% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/mummy-returns
  Rick and Evelyn O’Connell battle a resurrected Imhotep while racing to stop the ancient Scorpion King’s army from rising. Johnson opens the film as the warrior Mathayus and returns as a monstrous Scorpion King in the finale.
- **The Scorpion King** (2002) — Role: *Mathayus* · Directed by Chuck Russell · Worldwide Box Office: $165M · Critics Score: 41% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/scorpion-king
  In this prequel spin-off to The Mummy films, the assassin Mathayus is hired to kill the sorceress who protects the tyrant Memnon. His first leading role paid a record $5.5 million.
- **The Rundown** (2003) — Role: *Beck* · Directed by Peter Berg · Worldwide Box Office: $81M · Critics Score: 69% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/rundown
  A bounty hunter who dreams of opening a restaurant takes one last job: bringing his boss’s son (Seann William Scott) home from a lawless mining town in the Amazon. Arnold Schwarzenegger’s cameo plays as a passing of the action torch.
- **Walking Tall** (2004) — Role: *Chris Vaughn* · Directed by Kevin Bray · Critics Score: 26% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/walking-tall
  A former Special Forces soldier comes home to find his town overrun by a casino owner’s drugs and violence. He becomes sheriff to clean it up, with a two-by-four in hand.
- **Be Cool** (2005) — Role: *Elliot Wilhelm* · Directed by F. Gary Gray · Critics Score: 30% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/be-cool
  In the sequel to Get Shorty, Chili Palmer (John Travolta) moves from movies into the music business. Johnson steals scenes as Elliot, a bodyguard desperate to become an actor.
- **Doom** (2005) — Role: *Sarge* · Directed by Andrzej Bartkowiak · Worldwide Box Office: $58M · Critics Score: 18% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/doom
  A squad of Marines is sent to a research base on Mars after an experiment unleashes creatures on the scientists. Johnson plays Sarge, the squad’s hard-line commander, in this adaptation of the video game.
- **Gridiron Gang** (2006) — Role: *Sean Porter* · Directed by Phil Joanou · Critics Score: 42% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/gridiron-gang
  Based on a true story, a counselor at a juvenile detention camp builds a football team to give young offenders discipline and a second chance.
- **Southland Tales** (2006) — Role: *Boxer Santaros* · Directed by Richard Kelly · Critics Score: 40% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/southland-tales
  Richard Kelly’s sprawling satire of a near-future Los Angeles, where an amnesiac action star tied to a powerful political family is pulled into a conspiracy. It premiered in competition at Cannes.
- **Reno 911!: Miami** (2007) — Role: *Agent Rick “The Condor” Smith* · Directed by Ben Garant · Critics Score: 34% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/reno-911
  The hapless Reno sheriff’s deputies end up policing Miami Beach during a police convention. Johnson makes a cameo as a federal agent.
- **The Game Plan** (2007) — Role: *Joe Kingman* · Directed by Andy Fickman · Critics Score: 29% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/game-plan
  A self-absorbed star quarterback discovers he has an eight-year-old daughter and has to learn to be a father in the middle of the season.
- **Get Smart** (2008) — Role: *Agent 23* · Directed by Peter Segal · Worldwide Box Office: $231M · Critics Score: 51% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/get-smart
  Bumbling analyst Maxwell Smart (Steve Carell) gets his shot as a field agent alongside Agent 99 (Anne Hathaway). Johnson plays Agent 23, the spy agency’s star operative.
- **Planet 51** (2009) — Role: *Capt. Charles T. Baker (voice)* · Directed by Jorge Blanco, Javier Abad, Marcos Martínez · Critics Score: 23% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/planet-51
  An American astronaut lands on a planet he thinks is empty, only to find little green aliens living in a world that looks like 1950s suburbia, where he is the invader.
- **Race to Witch Mountain** (2009) — Role: *Jack Bruno* · Directed by Andy Fickman · Worldwide Box Office: $106M · Critics Score: 42% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/witch-mountain
  A Las Vegas cab driver finds two siblings with supernatural powers in his back seat and has to protect them from the government agents hunting them.
- **Faster** (2010) — Role: *Driver* · Directed by George Tillman, Jr. · Critics Score: 42% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/faster
  Just out of prison, a man sets out to kill everyone responsible for his brother’s murder, pursued by a veteran cop and a hitman. A lean, R-rated return to hard action.
- **The Other Guys** (2010) — Role: *Christopher Danson* · Directed by Adam McKay · Worldwide Box Office: $171M · Critics Score: 79% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/other-guys
  Two mismatched desk cops (Will Ferrell and Mark Wahlberg) get their chance when the precinct’s superstar detectives are suddenly out of the picture. Johnson and Samuel L. Jackson play those superstars.
- **Tooth Fairy** (2010) — Role: *Derek Thompson* · Directed by Michael Lembeck · Critics Score: 17% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/tooth-fairy
  A minor-league hockey enforcer who tells a child the tooth fairy isn’t real is sentenced to serve as one, wings and all.
- **Why Did I Get Married Too?** (2010) — Role: *Daniel Franklin* · Directed by Tyler Perry · Critics Score: 27% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/why-married-too
  Tyler Perry’s sequel follows four couples on a group getaway as their marriages start to crack. Johnson makes a brief cameo.
- **You Again** (2010) — Role: *Air Marshal* · Directed by Andy Fickman · Critics Score: 19% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/you-again
  A young woman discovers her brother is marrying the girl who bullied her in high school. Johnson has a cameo as an air marshal.
- **Fast Five** (2011) — Role: *Luke Hobbs* · Directed by Justin Lin · Worldwide Box Office: $626M · Critics Score: 78% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/fast-five
  Dom Toretto’s crew plans one last heist in Rio de Janeiro against a corrupt businessman, while relentless federal agent Luke Hobbs closes in. Johnson’s arrival turned the series into a global heist franchise.
- **Journey 2: The Mysterious Island** (2012) — Role: *Hank Parsons* · Directed by Brad Peyton · Worldwide Box Office: $335M · Critics Score: 45% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/journey-2
  A teenager and his stepfather follow a coded signal to a hidden island straight out of Jules Verne, full of giant creatures and lost treasure.
- **Empire State** (2013) — Role: *Det. James Ransome* · Directed by Dito Montiel · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/empire-state
  Based on a real 1982 armored-car depot robbery in New York, two childhood friends pull off the heist and draw the attention of a determined detective.
- **Fast & Furious 6** (2013) — Role: *Luke Hobbs* · Directed by Justin Lin · Worldwide Box Office: $789M · Critics Score: 71% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/ff6
  Hobbs recruits Dom’s crew to take down a team of mercenary drivers in Europe in exchange for pardons, and they discover Letty is alive and working for the other side.
- **G.I. Joe: Retaliation** (2013) — Role: *Roadblock* · Directed by Jon M. Chu · Worldwide Box Office: $376M · Critics Score: 29% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/gi-joe
  After the Joes are framed and nearly wiped out, Roadblock leads the survivors against Cobra and an impostor in the White House.
- **Pain & Gain** (2013) — Role: *Paul Doyle* · Directed by Michael Bay · Critics Score: 49% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/pain-gain
  Based on a true story, three Miami bodybuilders kidnap a wealthy businessman in a get-rich scheme that spirals out of control. Johnson plays a born-again ex-convict in Michael Bay’s dark crime comedy.
- **Snitch** (2013) — Role: *John Matthews* · Directed by Ric Roman Waugh · Critics Score: 57% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/snitch
  Inspired by true events, a father makes a deal with prosecutors to go undercover against a drug cartel to cut his son’s prison sentence.
- **Hercules** (2014) — Role: *Hercules* · Directed by Brett Ratner · Worldwide Box Office: $245M · Critics Score: 58% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/hercules
  Haunted by his past, the demigod leads a band of mercenaries hired to train an army in Thrace, where myth and politics collide.
- **Furious 7** (2015) — Role: *Luke Hobbs* · Directed by James Wan · Worldwide Box Office: $1.52B · Critics Score: 81% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/furious-7
  Deckard Shaw hunts Dom’s crew to avenge his brother, and the team takes on a global mission to recover a surveillance program called God’s Eye. The film is also the series’ farewell to Paul Walker.
- **Jem and the Holograms** (2015) — Role: *Himself* · Directed by Jon M. Chu · Critics Score: 22% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/jem
  A small-town teenager becomes an online music sensation and is swept into the industry with her sisters. Johnson appears briefly as himself.
- **San Andreas** (2015) — Role: *Ray Gaines* · Directed by Brad Peyton · Worldwide Box Office: $474M · Critics Score: 48% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/san-andreas
  When the San Andreas Fault triggers a massive earthquake, a Los Angeles fire department rescue pilot crosses a shattered California to save his daughter.
- **Central Intelligence** (2016) — Role: *Bob Stone* · Directed by Rawson Marshall Thurber · Worldwide Box Office: $217M · Critics Score: 71% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/central-intelligence
  A bullied high-school kid turned CIA agent pulls his old classmate, now an accountant (Kevin Hart), into a dangerous case. It launched his screen partnership with Hart.
- **Moana** (2016) — Role: *Maui (voice)* · Directed by John Musker, Ron Clements, Chris Williams, Don Hall · Worldwide Box Office: $691M · Critics Score: 95% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/moana
  A chief’s daughter sails beyond the reef to restore the heart of the goddess Te Fiti, with the reluctant help of the shape-shifting demigod Maui. Johnson sings “You’re Welcome”.
- **Baywatch** (2017) — Role: *Mitch Buchannon* · Directed by Seth Gordon · Critics Score: 17% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/baywatch
  A devoted lifeguard and a cocky new recruit (Zac Efron) uncover a criminal plot that threatens their beach, in this comedy take on the TV series.
- **Jumanji: Welcome to the Jungle** (2017) — Role: *Dr. Smolder Bravestone* · Directed by Jake Kasdan · Worldwide Box Office: $962M · Critics Score: 77% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/jumanji-wttj
  Four teenagers are pulled into a video game and become its adult avatars. Johnson plays the heroic archaeologist Bravestone, inhabited by a nervous, gangly gamer.
- **The Fate of the Furious** (2017) — Role: *Luke Hobbs* · Directed by F. Gary Gray · Worldwide Box Office: $1.24B · Critics Score: 67% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/fate-furious
  The cyberterrorist Cipher forces Dom to turn on his own crew, and Hobbs teams up with old enemy Deckard Shaw to bring him back.
- **Rampage** (2018) — Role: *Davis Okoye* · Directed by Brad Peyton · Worldwide Box Office: $428M · Critics Score: 51% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/rampage
  A primatologist races to save his gorilla friend, mutated to giant size by a genetic experiment, as other monsters tear through Chicago.
- **Skyscraper** (2018) — Role: *Will Sawyer* · Directed by Rawson Marshall Thurber · Worldwide Box Office: $305M · Critics Score: 48% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/skyscraper
  A former FBI hostage-rescue leader, now a security consultant, has to get into the world’s tallest building, set on fire by criminals, to save his family.
- **Fast & Furious Presents: Hobbs & Shaw** (2019) — Role: *Luke Hobbs* · Directed by David Leitch · Worldwide Box Office: $759M · Critics Score: 67% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/hobbs-shaw
  Hobbs and Deckard Shaw are forced to team up against a cybernetically enhanced terrorist (Idris Elba) to stop a deadly virus.
- **Fighting with My Family** (2019) — Role: *Himself* · Directed by Stephen Merchant · Critics Score: 93% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/fighting-family
  Based on the true story of WWE wrestler Paige and her wrestling family from Norwich, England. Johnson produced the film and appears as himself.
- **Jumanji: The Next Level** (2019) — Role: *Dr. Smolder Bravestone* · Directed by Jake Kasdan · Worldwide Box Office: $800M · Critics Score: 72% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/jumanji-next
  The friends go back into the game to rescue Spencer, but glitches put his grandfather into Bravestone. Johnson does a running impression of Danny DeVito.
- **Free Guy** (2021) — Role: *Bank Robber #2 (voice)* · Directed by Shawn Levy · Worldwide Box Office: $331M · Critics Score: 80% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/free-guy
  A bank teller discovers he is a background character in an open-world video game and decides to become its hero. Johnson lends a brief voice cameo.
- **Jungle Cruise** (2021) — Role: *Frank Wolff* · Directed by Jaume Collet-Serra · Critics Score: 62% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/jungle-cruise
  In 1916 a wisecracking riverboat captain takes a scientist (Emily Blunt) and her brother up the Amazon in search of a tree with legendary healing powers.
- **Red Notice** (2021) — Role: *John Hartley* · Directed by Rawson Marshall Thurber · Critics Score: 36% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/red-notice
  An FBI profiler is forced to team up with a rival art thief (Ryan Reynolds) to catch the world’s most wanted thief (Gal Gadot) in a hunt for Cleopatra’s jeweled eggs.
- **Black Adam** (2022) — Role: *Teth-Adam / Black Adam* · Directed by Jaume Collet-Serra · Worldwide Box Office: $393M · Critics Score: 38% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/black-adam
  Nearly 5,000 years after he was given the powers of the gods, Teth-Adam is freed from his tomb in Kahndaq and clashes with the Justice Society. A project he championed for more than a decade.
- **DC League of Super-Pets** (2022) — Role: *Krypto (voice)* · Directed by Jared Stern · Worldwide Box Office: $207M · Critics Score: 73% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/super-pets
  When the Justice League is captured, Superman’s dog Krypto has to lead a group of shelter animals with new superpowers to the rescue.
- **Fast X** (2023) — Role: *Luke Hobbs* · Directed by Louis Leterrier · Critics Score: 56% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/fast-x
  Dante Reyes, the son of the drug lord from Fast Five, sets out to destroy Dom’s family. Johnson returns as Hobbs in a mid-credits scene.
- **Moana 2** (2024) — Role: *Maui (voice)* · Directed by David Derrick Jr., Dana Ledoux Miller · Worldwide Box Office: $1.059B · Critics Score: 61% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/moana-2
  Three years after her first voyage, Moana answers a call from her ancestors and sets out to find a lost island, with Maui by her side again.
- **Red One** (2024) — Role: *Callum Drift* · Directed by Jake Kasdan · Critics Score: 30% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/red-one
  When Santa Claus is kidnapped, the head of North Pole security teams up with a cynical bounty hunter (Chris Evans) to save Christmas.
- **The Smashing Machine** (2025) — Role: *Mark Kerr* · Directed by Benny Safdie · Worldwide Box Office: $21M · Critics Score: 70% · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/smashing-machine
  Benny Safdie’s A24 drama follows MMA champion Mark Kerr through fights, addiction and his relationship with Dawn Staples (Emily Blunt). Johnson’s transformation earned him a Golden Globe nomination for Best Actor – Drama.
- **Jumanji: Open World** (2026) — Role: *Dr. Xander “Smolder” Bravestone* · Directed by Jake Kasdan · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/jumanji-3
  The final chapter of the Jumanji series, reuniting Johnson, Jack Black, Kevin Hart and Karen Gillan with director Jake Kasdan. Johnson also produces.
- **Moana** (2026) — Role: *Maui* · Directed by Thomas Kail · Worldwide Box Office: $324M · URL: __SITE_URL__/movies.html#movie/moana-live
  Disney’s live-action remake of the 2016 film, with Johnson playing the demigod Maui in person.
